findings.evidence: Lines 184, 223, 232; naming conventions: "to disambiguate ... it is necessary to describe some of the hypotheses. The word 'of' is used to separate these hypotheses."
findings.issue: `measureReal_trialLaw_acceptSet` reads as the real-valued counterpart of the unconditional `trialLaw_acceptSet` (line 184, RHS `∫⁻ min f (c*g) / c`), but it states `(∫ f)/c`, which needs `hle : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, f x ≤ c * g x` plus non-negativity and integrability. Its lintegral sibling at line 223 does carry the suffix (`trialLaw_acceptSet_of_ae_le`), so the pair is inconsistent and the general real-valued form has no name left.

findings.evidence: grep `violation` over upstream/mathlib/Mathlib: only Ordmap/Ordnode.lean and linter text, no declaration name uses it; naming conventions' symbol dictionary gives `lt` for `<` and `ne` for `≠`.
findings.fix: Name after the hypothesis statement in the standard dictionary, e.g. `acceptedLaw_ne_of_measure_lt_ne_zero` (`<` → `lt`, `≠ 0` → `ne_zero`), keeping the second measure condition as an unnamed side condition.
findings.issue: `acceptedLaw_ne_of_violation` names its hypotheses with the informal word "violation", which is not upstream terminology and does not say which relation fails; the hypotheses are `μ {x | c * g x < f x} ≠ 0` and `μ {x | 0 < f x ∧ f x ≤ c * g x} ≠ 0`.

findings.evidence: Line 70 `{s : Set (α × β)} (hs : MeasurableSet s)` vs line 95 `.restrict {p | p.2 ≤ a p.1}` — identical name prefix, different generality.
findings.fix: Put the set in the name, e.g. `map_fst_restrict_le_prod_uniformMeasure` or `map_fst_restrict_setOf_le_prod_uniformMeasure`.
findings.issue: `map_fst_restrict_prod_uniformMeasure` is named as the `ρ = uniformMeasure 0 1` specialisation of `map_fst_restrict_prod` (line 70, arbitrary `s`), but it is restricted to the specific set `{p | p.2 ≤ a p.1}`, which the name never mentions. A reader looking for the uniform case of the general lemma gets a strictly narrower statement.

findings.evidence: upstream/mathlib/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/Prod.lean:257 `@[simp] lemma map_fst_prod : Measure.map Prod.fst (μ.prod ν) = (ν univ) • μ`, inside `namespace Measure`; rubric: a declaration whose first explicit argument has a Mathlib type belongs in that type's namespace.
findings.fix: Declare them in `MeasureTheory.Measure` (as `Measure.map_fst_restrict_prod`), so `ν.map_fst_restrict_prod ρ hs` elaborates and the lemma can be upstreamed without renaming.
findings.issue: `map_fst_restrict_prod` (and likewise `map_fst_restrict_prod_uniformMeasure`, line 94) takes `(ν : Measure α)` as its first explicit argument and is pure Mathlib-level measure theory, but sits in the `EpsilonEridani` namespace; the upstream lemma of exactly this shape is `MeasureTheory.Measure.map_fst_prod`.

summary: Most names are conventional, but one name hides the hypotheses that make it true and breaks the convention its own sibling follows, one uses non-upstream jargon for its hypotheses, and two generic measure lemmas are filed outside the Mathlib namespace their first explicit argument dictates.
